guard: a subject wildcard with no literal form in the corpus still reaches the sections that name its base subject
completionMarker: ✓ 4 — an unknown page fails loud and lists what is available
why: This suite sat RED on main and nothing anywhere executed it: `smoke:docs` is in the `check`
root only, absent from `smoke:ci`, and absent from every workflow. A lane running `smoke:ci`
locally saw green and CI saw green. Reachability from a root is not execution, and
`gate-inventory` grades the former.
WHAT WAS ACTUALLY RED, and it was neither a code defect nor the hypothesis on offer. The cell
asserted that `$SYS.>` surfaces the SPEC section documenting $SYS, in the default five hits. It
went red on 2026-08-12, when `fix(auth): renew the $SYS creds by rotation` gave docs/cli.md and
docs/identity-and-auth.md operational $SYS prose. Replayed against the bundle at that commit's
parent the spec ranks 4th; at the commit itself two new sections appear and it ranks 6th. The
standing hypothesis -- that a ~19k-character changelog row in SPEC.md diluted the spec's term
frequencies -- is FALSE, and cheap to falsify: dropping both giant rows moves every score by
under 0.06 and changes no ordering at all.
So the assertion was a CORPUS fact pinned as if it were a CODE property, and it was never held
up by any mechanism -- it was true only while no other page happened to say $SYS. It was going
to break on someone else's docs edit, and it did.
A MECHANISM WAS TRIED AND REJECTED, on measurement rather than taste. Emitting the namespace
prefix a wildcard names (`$SYS.>` -> `$SYS.`) does rank the spec first, because exactly one
place in the corpus writes `$SYS.` -- but it scores PUNCTUATION: every single `mesh.` in the
docs is the word "mesh" ending a sentence, across 14 pages, so `mesh.*` swapped its useful
hits for the pages with the most sentence-final periods. There is no signal here to rank on,
so the cells assert reachability and stop claiming rank.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, and this suite is on the wrong side of it. `docs.smoke.ts` imports
`@cotal-ai/connector-core`, a package specifier that resolves to `dist`. A mutation in `src`
with a bare `tsx` command would be VOID ON ARRIVAL -- the mutant would sit in `src` while the
suite graded an untouched `dist`, and the kill rate would measure module resolution rather
than the guard. The command therefore carries the package build. This also means the suite is
only honest about `src` when something has built: in CI it runs after the Build step for that
reason.
NOT GRADED, and named rather than implied: the new `every hit names $SYS` cell has no
realistic single-token mutation. It is a companion that stops the length cell being satisfied
by noise, not a guard with its own failure mode; the mutations that empty or pollute the
result set are caught by the two cells below or by pre-existing cells, and manufacturing a
third to make it gradable would be a mutation written for the report.
A REVIEWER'S SURVIVOR, FOUND AND CLOSED IN THE SAME ROUND, and it is the sharpest thing here.
The repair replaced "the spec is in the default five" with "the spec is in the first ten" and
called that reachability. It is not: the spec ranks SIXTH, so the new cell carried four slots of
slack against the same afternoon's corpus, a docs wave adding four higher-scoring $SYS sections
would have reddened it the same way, and any hardcoded cut of six or more left every cell green.
A corpus fact pinned as a code property does not stop being one because the window got wider.
The reachability cell is now UNWINDOWED and asserts no rank whatsoever, and the limit argument is
graded separately against a COUNT, which nothing in the corpus can move.
MEASURED SURVIVOR IN A CELL THAT IS NOT MINE, reported rather than fixed: disabling the dotted
segment expansion entirely (`if (t.includes(".")) for (const seg of ...)` -> `if (false)`)
leaves the suite GREEN. The cell named "a dotted path matches on its segments" only asserts
`searchDocs("cotal.schema.json").length > 0`, which the raw whole-token match satisfies on its
own, so it does not test segment matching. Out of scope here; flagged for whoever owns it.
MARKER IS UPSTREAM ON PURPOSE. The suite's terminal line sits AFTER the mutated region, so every
real kill stops before it and the tool cannot tell a kill from a run that died at cell 1 -- it
graded both mutations INCONCLUSIVE for exactly that reason. The marker named here is section 4's,
printed before the search section, so reaching it proves the run got as far as the region under
test. The per-section marks were added in the same change: this suite reported one word for some
thirty assertions, which is also why nobody could see it was red.
RESTORE IS INCOMPLETE HERE AND IT IS THIS CONFIG'S FAULT, not the tool's. mutation-proof restores
the file it edited -- `src` -- and verifies that restore. It cannot know the command's build step
copied the mutant into `dist`, which is what this suite actually loads. So the tree is clean and
`dist` still holds the last mutant: a bare `pnpm smoke:docs` immediately afterwards grades a
mutant nobody put there, and it looks like a fresh regression. Observed, not theorised. Within
this config it is self-correcting because the command rebuilds first; run the build once by hand
after a session with it.

It is also the mutation that would silently restore the red -- the repair is that the spec is REACHABLE, and a hardcoded window is exactly what makes reachable and ranked the same claim again.

mutations.cell: a limit of one returns one section
mutations.note: A REVIEWER FOUND THIS AS A SURVIVOR AND IT IS THE POINT OF THE ROUND. The previous cell asked for the spec inside the first TEN hits; the spec sits at rank six, so the assertion was carrying four slots of slack against one afternoon's corpus and any hardcoded cut of six or more left every cell green. Mutation 2 above only killed because five happened to be below the spec's current rank -- it was grading the corpus, which is the exact defect this whole config exists to remove, one layer down. The reachability cell is now UNWINDOWED and claims no rank at all, and the limit argument is asserted against a COUNT instead, which no corpus fact can drift.

mutations.name: the limit is not applied at all, so every query returns the whole ranked corpus
mutations.expectRed: a limit of one returns one section
mutations.cell: a limit of one returns one section
mutations.note: The other direction, and it is the one that reads as harmless: nothing is lost, everything is found, and a docs tool that answers a search with sixty-five sections has blown the context it was called to protect. The reachability cell CANNOT see this -- an unwindowed query is exactly what it asks for -- which is why the count cells are its pair rather than a duplicate of it.
